title: US approves $2.1 billion Patriot missile sale to Ukraine
note: Washington has approved a sale of Patriot interceptors reported at 500 missiles and $2.1 billion, while Ukraine's president warns deliveries may take years. It eases a shortage of the only weapon that reliably stops Russian ballistic missiles, but the delivery lag leaves a gap.
limitations: Approval of a potential sale is not a delivery schedule, and the timeline is disputed between Kyiv and NATO officials. Drafted by an automated daily job from the linked report; not yet reviewed.

title: Iranian lawmakers call for withdrawal from the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty
note: Al Jazeera reports Iranian lawmakers are urging an exit from the NPT. Observers quoted say withdrawal would not itself mean building a weapon, but it would end treaty inspections and raise the risk of renewed war with the US.
limitations: A call by lawmakers is not government policy, and the source gives no sign of a formal decision. Drafted by an automated daily job from the linked report; not yet reviewed.

note: Al Jazeera reports Iran warns any response to an attack would be unrestricted while mediators work for a deal. The wider-theater threat raises the stakes for Gulf states and shipping if talks fail.

title: More than 300,000 people displaced since March remain displaced in Lebanon
note: The UN aid coordination office says the humanitarian crisis in Lebanon is far from over, with over 300,000 people still internally displaced since early March. Prolonged displacement shows how far conflict damage persists beyond active fighting.
limitations: The figure is a UN estimate from a news brief with no breakdown of causes or locations. Drafted by an automated daily job from the linked report; not yet reviewed.

title: US, Japan and South Korea reaffirm complete denuclearization goal as Pyongyang objects
note: The three foreign ministers pledged complete denuclearization of North Korea and signed an Arctic-Pacific cooperation memorandum, while North Korea called a related multinational statement on sanctions a strategic failure. The hardened positions come as possible US-North Korea talks are discussed.
limitations: Joint statements show positions, not any change in North Korean capabilities or willingness to negotiate. Drafted by an automated daily job from the linked report; not yet reviewed.

title: More than 28 million people in DR Congo lack enough food, IPC alert says
note: The IPC food security monitor says hunger in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is deepening amid conflict, Ebola and climate shocks, and is expected to rise in coming months. Food stress in the east compounds displacement and weakens state capacity.
limitations: IPC figures are modeled estimates, and access limits in conflict areas reduce data quality. Drafted by an automated daily job from the linked report; not yet reviewed.
